content.title: About
content.content: Chicken necks and ribs are meat portions of the bird often used in dishes that require long simmering. They are rich in collagen, giving soups and stews a deep flavor and aroma. When cooked properly they become tender and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken necks and ribs are a staple in traditional broths and soups because they add richness.
In many Asian cuisines they are fried until crispy and served as a snack.
The collagen they contain is beneficial for joints and skin.
Chicken ribs can be sold whole or cut into individual pieces.
Slow braising makes the bones separate easily from the meat.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Provides essential amino acids needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Collagen source
items.content: Supports joint health, skin elasticity, and hair strength.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: Compared with other cuts, necks and ribs have a relatively low fat level, especially when skin is removed.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B6 and B12, which aid nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth and food poisoning.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the product is pre‑salted, consider total sodium intake.

items.title: Bones
items.content: Small bones can be a choking hazard for children and should be removed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Necks and ribs are ideal for slow braising, stewing, roasting, or making broth. They can be marinated then seared to a golden crust, or added to casseroles. Before cooking, trim excess fat and skin for a leaner result.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C up to 6 months. Discard if any off‑odor or slimy texture appears.
